answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks that require scarce, independently verified resources, such as a bonded deposit or a signed delivery receipt. The ledger releases payment and reputation only after a randomly chosen verifier confirms the result; disputes forfeit the bond. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply scarce deposits or valid receipts, while coordinating them risks many bonds at once. A jade shipment tracked across an atlas of routes in the tundra still needs real custody evidence, not a crowd of fresh accounts.
